card.situation:
U.S. Embassy Djibouti solicitation for firm-fixed-price gardening and grounds maintenance services at the DCMR compound, requiring all labor, equipment, and compliance with local Djibouti law and Embassy security requirements.
Reached the owner because NAICS 561730 matches exactly and the firm holds directly relevant grounds maintenance past performance — but the place of performance is Djibouti, Africa, triggering the owner's 200-mile distance rule.
reasons_for: NAICS 561730 is an exact match and the firm's grounds maintenance past performance (mowing, trimming, irrigation, landscaping) maps directly to the core scope [d698e029-6ae5b154-p10-c7d47434].
OSHA 30-certified supervisors and a CMMS-based QC inspection program satisfy the supervision, safety meeting, and monthly reporting requirements [d698e029-6ae5b154-p9-0eca90a2].

The firm holds multiple FAR-governed federal contracts (GSA, DoD, VA) demonstrating full compliance with the standard FAR and fixed-price contract clauses required here [d698e029-6ae5b154-p16-da5fc11c].
reasons_against: Place of performance is Djibouti — approximately 8,000+ miles from Oklahoma City — which is a hard violation of owner rule [rc-distance] prohibiting bids over 200 miles from Oklahoma City [d698e029-6ae5b154-p15-52bf2b4c].

The firm has no Defense Base Act (DBA) insurance, no international experience, and no presence in Djibouti or at any U.S. Embassy overseas, leaving critical proposal requirements unmet [d698e029-6ae5b154-p29-7e72b7dc].
The firm holds no Djibouti local licenses or permits, has no plan to obtain them, and has no experience complying with foreign country labor laws or DOSAR 652.242-73 [d698e029-6ae5b154-p30-93707aaf].

drafts.capability_statement:
Red Cedar Facility Services is a Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) headquartered in Oklahoma City, OK, registered in SAM.gov and operating under NAICS 561730 (Landscaping Services) — the exact NAICS code assigned to this solicitation.

Red Cedar provides grounds maintenance services to federal and state government customers, including turf and grass care, mowing, trimming, irrigation monitoring, herbicide application, landscaping, and debris removal. Our past performance includes grounds maintenance at a U.S. Air Force cantonment area (Tinker AFB, 72 ABW), custodial and grounds services at the Oklahoma City Federal Building (GSA Region 7), and housekeeping services at the VA Oklahoma City — all performed under firm-fixed-price, FAR-governed contracts.

Our workforce of 38 W-2 employees is supervised by OSHA 30-certified site supervisors. Quality control inspections are logged in a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS), supporting the monthly summary reporting requirement in this solicitation. We provide all required equipment — mowers, trimmers, rakes, shovels, clippers, hoses, and sprayers — and enforce PPE compliance on every work site.

Red Cedar has demonstrated consistent performance on federal installations requiring personnel vetting and security access coordination, and holds a strong record of FAR and fixed-price contract compliance across GSA, DoD, and VA customers.

Contracting Officer: we welcome the opportunity to discuss how our grounds maintenance capabilities can serve the DCMR compound in Djibouti.

deadlines.set_aside_note: The notice has no set-aside. Red Cedar Facility Services can claim WOSB, EDWOSB, and SBA set-asides, but this is an unrestricted solicitation — the firm is eligible to bid on unrestricted awards, so no set-aside barrier exists. However, owner rule [rc-distance] prohibits bids over 200 miles from Oklahoma City, and the place of performance is Djibouti — far outside that radius. Additionally, owner rule [rc-base] requires a minimum 12-month base period, which cannot be confirmed from the text. The firm should NOT bid due to the distance rule violation (Djibouti is thousands of miles from Oklahoma City, OK).
